Mr. Justice D.Dash
 Mr. Justice G. Satapathy
 Order
Order No. 14.11.2023
 01. 1.
This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement  (virtual/physical) mode.

2. The Petitioner by filing this writ petition has invoked the jurisdiction of this Court under Ariticle-226 & 227 of the Constitution of India has prayed for quashing the order dated 30.06.2033 passed by the Opposite Party No.4 in Misc.Case No.05 of 2023 with further direction to the Opposite Parties more particularly Opposite Party No.4 to disburse compensation in favour of the Petitioner and his family members for the acquisition of their land as also the standing tree as described.

3. Heard Mr. N. Lenka, learned Counsel for the Petitioner and Mr. G.N. Rout, learned Addl.
Standing Counsel for the State as well as Mr. P.K. Parhi, learned Dy. Solicitor General being assisted by Mr. B.K. Pardhi, learned Central Govt. Counsel for the Union of India.
4. Keeping in view the submission made, the averments taken in the petition as also documents annexed thereto being gone through, it is seen that the Petitioner raising the grievance for non-payment of adequate compensation for acquisition of // 2 // their land for the purpose of Talcher-Bimlagarh New Broad Gauge Rail Link Project, Talcher had approached this Court in W.P.(C) No.33234 of 2022.
This Court while disposing the said writ petition had directed the Opposite Party No.4 to consider the representation filed by the Petitioner and pass appropriate order.
The Opposite Party No.4 in obedience to the order of this Court sitting over to consider the representation filed by the Petitioner had called for the field report from the officials.

The Collector on consideration of the report called for the purpose has found that the land belonging to the father of the Petitioner and other co-sharers having been acquired by the Railway Authorities in due process of law, there has been assessment of compensation and the compensation amount despite Antaryami Sahoo vs Union Of India & Others ....

sentences.text:
Opposite ... on 14 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148780102/
1 notice being not received by the Petitioner and others as are entitled, that has been lying being deposited in the Special Treasury, Talcher 21.03.2016.

It has further been found out that the claim of the Petitioner for compensation concerning the land measuring Ac.0.38 decimals under Plot No.622 and Ac.2.84 under Plot No.607 and Khata Nos.359 and 362, kisam-Taila-II and Gochar respectively are Government lands and the Petitioner being an encroacher, no compensation for those lands are payable.

5. The Petitioner states that as per clause-10 of Odisha Resettlement and Rehabilitation Policy,
2006, he is entitled to the benefits.
On a plain reading of clause-10 of the Policy in place, it would be clear that the benefit under the policy is go to the landless and homestead less encroachers.

The Petitioner since does not come within the definition of "landless" as defined in Odisha Prevention of Land Encroachment Act, 1972, and as such is not entitled to the benefits since the Petitioner's // 3 // main claim as advanced in the writ petition is devoid of merit, we are not inclined to entertain this writ petition.

entities.text: Odisha Prevention of Land Encroachment Act, 1972

sentences.text: 6. Accordingly, the writ Petition stands dismissed.
No order as to cost.
